steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease an 8-inch square pan.
Sift flour, baking powder, salt, and 1/4 teaspoon of cinnamon into a medium bowl. Stir 2 tablespoons white sugar and remaining 2 teaspoons cinnamon together in a small bowl.

Mix brown sugar, 1/2 cup white sugar, and melted butter together in a large bowl with a wooden spoon until smooth. Stir in egg and vanilla. Blend in flour mixture until just combined, then stir in apple and walnuts. Spread mixture evenly into the prepared pan and sprinkle cinnamon-sugar mixture over top.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top springs back when lightly pressed, 25 to 30 minutes. Let cool completely in the pan before cutting into 16 squares.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple Squares
raw_recipe.description: These easy apple squares are baked with brown sugar, cinnamon, and walnuts for a sweet, warmly spiced dessert with a cinnamon-sugar topping.

video.description: Apples, nuts, and cinnamon make an amazing dessert treat.

review.reviewBody: Here are few tips that I learn from doing that recipe. First, I tripled most of the recipe, except for the topping. I baked it into big rectangular corning ware dish (about 16" x 9). I added a touch of almond extract. It gives it a nice taste. When baked, I topped it with a touch of icing sugar. It looked great. DO NOT over cook. I baked them for 30-35 minutes. These squares are better when they are moist. Do as the recipe says. Do not use a toothpick to judge if bake or not as it will come out as if it was not baked. Hope this help!

Just made these this afternoon and the kids had already eaten half the pan before the bars finished cooling! These are really tasty. I doubled the recipe (but I cut down BOTH sugars to approx. 3/4c each) and increased the apples to 2 large chopped apples (just over 2c). Left out the nuts. The bars were still sweet enough and don't require any frosting (although the caramel drizzle one reviewer suggested would be delish). Did not double the cinn/sugar topping. Baked in 9x13 pan for 33 minutes. My daughter said to save this recipe and we'll definitely make again soon!

I didn't try these so I have to write this review based on Hubs' report. He said these were the kind of thing he could eat till he got sick on they were that good. Five stars, he said, and better than his all-time favorite butterscotch cookies. Wow! I used Granny Smith apple, left out the nuts at his request and glazed them (right on top of the cinnamon sugar topping) with a butterscotch glaze I kind of just threw together as an experiment: 2 T. each of butter, brown sugar and cream, boiled for a couple of minutes, added about 1/2 tsp. vanilla, then more cream and powdered sugar till desired consistency. These are chewy, subtley cinnamony and appley with a butterscotch finish (his words, not mine). Definitely a make again!

Moist and chewy just like brownies! So yummy and easy to make that I baked these two days in a row for both daughters' school apple festivals. Used 1 whole apple (1 cup diced). Before serving, dusted with powdered sugar to make it look more attractive. Brought home empty plates both nights!

Wow, this satisfied a craving! I doubled the recipe to fit a 9x13” pan. (Made 24 squares, so the recipe is accurate!) Grated the apple instead of chopping (texture preference), reduced the sugar to 1.5 cups + 2 tbsp molasses, left out the nuts (dental surgery=sore mouth), then lightly dusted the top w/ cinnamon sugar I had from a previous recipe (halve the cinnamon sugar that this calls for—you likely won’t need as much!) The mixture is stiff, almost dough-like, but resist adding liquid here or it’ll be runny! Baked for 30 min, until the side of the spatula bounces back when pressed the surface—this is SUPPOSED to be moist. Allowed it to cool before jabbing it into squares with a spatula (look, there’s probably a better way of cutting these…but I’m just being honest here. I jabbed em. Turned out fine.) YOM. Apple pie flavour, brownie texture. Husband promptly inhaled 4+ (?) squares so...was a good call doubling this. Thanks so much for sharing the recipe—came in clutch and became an instant favourite!

My family loved this recipe for sure! It is like eating an apple pie in cake form. I sprayed the spatula and this made spreading the dough to easy. I sprayed the dough with cooking spray and the sugar mixture stuck easily. I only used one teaspoon of cinnamon in the white sugar mixture. Absolutely delicious!

Super yummy! I followed the advice of others and doubled the recipe (except the sugar topping) using a 9x13 pan. I didn't follow the directions as written but just combined the wet ingredients and sugars, cutting back on white sugar some, and then separately mixed the dry ingredients together (half whole wheat flour and added 1/2 tsp nutmeg). Then I combined it all before adding apples (2 cups total ambrosia and granny smith), walnuts, and a handful of craisins. Once cooled I piped a maple glaze on top. Very nice!

Loved it! I made a double batch in a 9x13” pan. I needed to cook it for 35 minutes. I used extra apples cutting them into small chunks. I did not put nuts in them as I’m taking them to a seniors home. I think pecans would add to the yummyness. The way this recipe is written is confusing; the topping directions and ingredients are in the middle of the cookie ingredients. It would be clearer if the topping was separated under the bar ingredients.

It was very tasty. I made 1.5 recipe in a 9×13 glass pan, used a little bit less than 2/3 cup of white sugar plus a tbsp of molasses, 1.5 cups apples, 2 tbsp of apple juice and 0.5 tsp of cinnamon. I topped it with a cream cheese glaze (30 gm cream cheese, 45 gm butter, 1 tbsp milk, 2/3 cup icing sugar, 1/8 tsp of each salt and vanilla)

I made the recipe exactly as written, except my dish was 8x8 instead of 9x9. I baked it at 350 for 30 min. I used a full apple, however much that was. The finished product was very moist. I can understand how some reviewers didn't like that because it's not what they expected, but the taste is fantastic and the people I served it to went back for seconds. That's a hit in my book. The cinnamon/sugar topping is too much. Cut it in half. Otherwise I recommend sticking to the recipe.

Video instructs you to use a Granny Smith apple and finely chopped toasted walnuts. I would make again with attempts at reducing the sugar, first trying 3/4 of total for topping and then maybe next attempt, trying to reduce the amount in the batter. That being said, everyone loved it even though it's a sugar bomb!

Had a box of Dolly Parton blondie bar mix kicking around so used that, substituting chunky apple sauce for the oil called for on the box. Sauteed 2 chopped apples in butter, cinnamon and walnuts, stirring half in the batter and spreading the other half on top before baking as directed. A scoop of ice cream never had a better friend.
These are delicious, my husband loves them. We aren’t walnut fans so didn’t include, everything else as listed. I doubled and baked in a 13 x 9 pan. Yummy!!!!
I didn't change one thing. (except I didn't have walnuts so I used pecans) and it is delicious! Items you have on hand, easy prep and quick to make. Thank you!
Nice flavor and chewy. Cinnamon sugar on top could be reduced.
I tried it with gluten free ingredients. It did effect it negatively. Then again I am very used to baking and eating gluten free. I used oat flour.
We love these bars. It’s so easy to make and so delicious! I added extra apples, but otherwise made as directed (using an 11” x 7” glass dish). This is definitely a keeper.
Baked this exactly as written. This recipe is tasty, easy, and I plan on baking this again.

Made the recipe as written and was pleasantly surprised. I don't think I was expecting the texture. They had the chew of a brownie, and I liked that. The only changes I would make is maybe toast the nuts before adding them, and a little less of the cinnamon sugar topping. It didn't all get absorbed, and there was a fine layer of loose sugar after they were baked. But it's a keeper!
These are so good and so easy to make. I did add 1 Tbsp of cream as suggested and doubled the amount of apples. Gone in 60 seconds! I'm making them again with pears.
